title: workplan_checkpoint input (native surface)
description: Record a checkpoint bound to the current plan manifest. Without merge=true this replaces the whole checkpoint (omitted lists become empty); to update it, pass merge=true or read the current checkpoint first. Pass expectedHash = the stateHash from your latest read or successful write.

id.description: Workplan id; normalized to lowercase [a-z0-9-] (max 80) before use.

summary.description: Checkpoint summary. Required unless merge=true. Refused when, trimmed, it is null or undefined or starts with 'null ' or 'undefined ' (a withheld resume value, D.4.3).

nextAction.description: Next action recorded in the checkpoint. Required unless merge=true. Refused like summary.

expectedHash.description: stateHash from the latest read; binds the write to that exact state.

merge.description: D.4.3 (approved 2026-10-01): keep the stored checkpoint's value of every omitted field (summary, nextAction, phase/step position, blockers, recentValidation, guardrails, references); given fields replace theirs. A missing or unreadable checkpoint merges as an empty one; a legacy v1 checkpoint's fields are carried over. The result binds the current plan state like any checkpoint.

appendValidation.description: D.4.3 (approved 2026-10-01): line(s) appended to recentValidation after merge or replacement; blank lines and exact duplicates of a line already present are skipped.

x-shiori-rules.native: Native existing-state writes require the current stateHash — pass expectedHash set to the stateHash from your last successful write, or re-read with workplan_resume or workplan_inspect first

x-shiori-rules.when: summary or nextAction, trimmed, is null or undefined or starts with 'null ' or 'undefined ' (case-sensitive; D.4.3)
x-shiori-rules.native: Checkpoint <field> starts with null/undefined, which is how workplan_resume shows a withheld field of a stale or legacy checkpoint, not its value — read the stored checkpoint first (the file named in the resume instruction), or pass merge=true and omit <field> to keep the stored value
x-shiori-rules.core: Checkpoint <field> starts with null/undefined, which is how workplan_resume shows a withheld field of a stale or legacy checkpoint, not its value — read the stored checkpoint first (the file named in the resume instruction), or pass merge=true and omit <field> to keep the stored value

x-shiori-rules.when: merge == true, summary or nextAction omitted, and no readable stored checkpoint has it (D.4.3; checked during preparation)
x-shiori-rules.native: merge=true keeps the stored <field>, but there is no readable stored checkpoint — pass <field>
x-shiori-rules.core: merge=true keeps the stored <field>, but there is no readable stored checkpoint — pass <field>

x-shiori-core-surface: The standalone CLI/core surface additionally accepts optional 'workspaceRoot' (string); the native surface rejects it as an unrecognized key. The allOf conditions are native-surface rules; the core surface keeps expectedHash optional for legacy direct calls (a concurrent change must still be detected), and uses the 'core' messages in x-shiori-rules.
